This note states no explicit met/beat/missed verdict. The result is classified here as in line because 47% of Kenanga's own full-year forecast at the half-year mark is close to a straight-line pace; against consensus, at 41%, it would read as a shortfall. The classification is this dashboard's inference, not Kenanga's stated wording. It does not change the Kenanga Signal, which does not depend on it.

The report confirms this is an upgrade and states the TP rise as +11%, but doesn't print the previous rating letter or exact prior TP in the extract pulled for this build — shown here as Market Perform to Outperform and RM0.53 (both inferred: the rating from the standard one-notch-upgrade convention, the TP by dividing RM0.59 by 1.11) rather than as printed figures. Worth confirming against the full PDF.

The extract pulled for this build confirms a rating downgrade and states the prior TP (RM1.91) explicitly, but does not print the specific prior rating letter — shown here as Outperform to Market Perform based on the report's consistently bullish framing of the long-term thesis elsewhere in the note, not a printed figure. Worth confirming against the full PDF.

Kenanga's own filename for this report is dated 260808 (8 Aug) while the report was published in the 28 Aug 2026 bundle — a typo in the source file name, not an error in this dashboard. The report content is dated 28 Aug.

Kenanga's own headline calls the half 'Good 1H, In Line', while the body notes core profit at 42% of the house forecast and 41% of consensus — slightly behind a 50% straight-line pace. The classification here follows Kenanga's stated 'In Line' verdict rather than the percentage, but the two readings differ and the note is worth opening directly.

This report's stated 'top pick' is DIALOG, a stock with no standalone Kenanga report in today's bundle; DIALOG's and KEYFIELD's rating/TP figures below are as quoted in this sector piece and have not been independently verified against a DIALOG- or KEYFIELD-specific report today.

The Kenanga Signal on this row reads None stated even though the report's Investment case paragraph opens "We continue to like MBMR for: (i) its strong earnings visibility...". Under rules/signals.md §2 that phrasing is thesis language, not a pick declaration — the report names MBMR neither a Top Pick nor a sector pick nor the most attractive among peers, and its own peer table on page 4 carries MBMR at MARKET PERFORM with -6% downside against five OUTPERFORM-rated peers. Separately, the report is internally inconsistent on dividend yield: page 1 and the financial tables both show a 9.0% net dividend yield for FY26F/FY27F, while the Investment case paragraph on page 2 says "attractive dividend yield of about 10%". Both figures are quoted as printed; neither has been reconciled.

The Kenanga Signal on this row reads None stated because KJTS's own Company Update contains no pick declaration — only an 'Investment thesis' paragraph beginning 'We like KJTS for...'. Kenanga's separate Market Strategy note in the same 3 September bundle does list KJTS (with SAMAIDEN) under 'Sector Top picks' for Renewable Energy & Energy Efficiency (Exhibit 11). That statement sits in a different report and is recorded on the Market Strategy row, not inferred onto this one.

This sector note states ratings and target prices for IOICORP, KLK, HSPLANT, TSH, PPB and UMCCA, none of which has a standalone Kenanga report in today's bundle. Those figures are as quoted in this sector piece and have not been independently verified against stock-specific reports today.

This strategy note states ratings and target prices for a large number of stocks across the coverage universe (including QL, MAYBANK, HLBANK, SIMEPROP, ABMB, BURSA, YTLPOWR, DIALOG, KEYFIELD, HSPLANT and others), none of which has a standalone Kenanga report in today's bundle. Those figures are as quoted in this strategy piece and have not been independently verified against stock-specific reports today. Note also that the PDF filename is dated 260902 while the document's own header is dated 03 September 2026; it is published in the 3 September bundle and listed in that day's Ideas of the Day.

Three data-quality points on this row, all internal to Kenanga's own PDF. (1) The report states its earnings revision three different ways: the front-page summary says 'We raise FY27F-FY28F earnings by 11%-20%', the Forecasts paragraph says 8% and 15% respectively, and the Summary Earnings Table's Earnings Revision row says 4.6% and 15.8%. All three are reproduced in the takeaways rather than one being silently chosen. (2) The front page gives YTD FY27 wins as 'c.RM150m' while the order-book paragraph gives 'c.RM143m'. (3) The peer-comparison table on page 4 is stale — it shows KEEMING at a last price of RM1.70 and a target price of RM1.80, against RM2.41 and RM2.84 in the same document. Separately, the previous target price of RM2.00 shown on this row is NOT stated in today's PDF: it is taken from an NST report of Kenanga's 26 June 2026 note (Outperform, TP raised to RM2.00 from RM1.80), and reconciles with today's arithmetic — RM2.84 is 22x the FY28F core EPS of 12.9 sen, and 18x the pre-revision FY28F EPS of about 11.2 sen is roughly RM2.00. Finally, the PDF filename is dated 260903 while the document's own header reads 04 September 2026 and it is published in the 4 September bundle. The 52-week range shown is stockanalysis.com's (RM0.60-RM2.58); Kenanga's own stock-information box gives RM0.38-RM2.56, where the RM0.38 low corresponds to the February 2026 IPO price rather than a traded low.

The sum-of-parts table on page 2 values the construction segment at RM4,540.5m on a stated basis of '16x FY27 PER', while the Valuations paragraph on page 1 says the construction target PER was rerated to 18x from 16x. The two are inconsistent within the same document and Kenanga does not reconcile them; both are reported here rather than one being chosen. Separately, the RM3.08 share price is Kenanga's own quoted figure and equals the 52-week high shown both in its stock-information box and on stockanalysis.com, but the Bloomberg-sourced overbought table in the same day's Kenanga Today digest already prints KERJAYA at a last price of RM3.100 with a 30-day high of RM3.150 — so the report's price is a snapshot slightly behind the market.

The placement price is reported two different ways by two sources published on the same day, and both are correct at different stages. Farm Fresh's own announcement, as reported by The Star on 3 September and used by TA Securities in its 4 September note, gives an illustrative issue price of RM1.824, a 10% discount to the five-day VWAMP of RM2.0267 as at 2 September. Kenanga's note says the price 'has subsequently been fixed at RM1.95/share, representing a 3.2% discount to the 5-day VWAMP of RM2.0134/share'. The difference is the illustrative announcement price versus the subsequently fixed book-built price, against VWAMPs struck on different reference dates — not a contradiction in the underlying facts. Kenanga's own conviction language on this row is an investment-case line ('We like FFB for' its RTD milk leadership, ice cream foray and product innovation), which is not a pick declaration, so the signal reads None stated.

Named as the day's Company Update by both the Kenanga Today digest and the 8 September bundle page heading, but no HLIND report has been published: the bundle's Company Update slot holds GAMUDA-260907-CU, the previous day's report already carried on this board's 7 September date, and HLIND returns 404 under every filename convention in rules/signals.md §6. Shown as a pending row rather than hidden; no figures have been guessed.

Three internal inconsistencies inside this single PDF are reported here as printed rather than resolved. (1) Page 1 says the officer-in-charge 'will carry out the 5-year plan already set out in motion' while page 2 says the interim head 'will complete some of the 3-year plan already set out in motion'; the strategy is elsewhere described as spanning 2026-2030, which is five years. (2) Page 1 gives current total bed capacity as '~4,000' in one sentence and, in the next, sets the FY26 target as a 4%-5% increase 'from 3,900 beds'. (3) The Summary Earnings Table shows EV/EBITDA of 11.4x for FY26F and 10.4x for FY27F, while the Peers Table in the same document shows KPJ HEALTHCARE at 16.3x one-year forward and 15.2x two-year forward - a difference of about 45% on a metric of the same name, which the report does not reconcile. Separately, the 52-week range in Kenanga's own stock-information box (H RM3.52, L RM2.37) differs slightly from the market data used in this row's range columns (stockanalysis.com: RM3.53 / RM2.34).

Five points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The downgrade direction conflicts with Kenanga's own earlier note. This report is headed MARKET PERFORM with a down arrow and says it is 'adjusting our call from OUTPERFORM to MARKET PERFORM', but Kenanga's Plastic Packaging sector update of 15 July 2026 had already downgraded 'SCIENTX (MP, TP: RM3.91) from OUTPERFORM to MARKET PERFORM following share price action' - at the same RM3.91 target. Between the two, the peer tables in Kenanga's own TGUAN and BPPLAS results notes of 27 August show SCIENTEX BHD as OP at RM3.70/RM3.91, and no note upgrading it back to OUTPERFORM was publicly retrievable. The two documents cannot both be right; both are recorded here. (2) The segmental table does not add up in its full-year columns. Packaging plus Property gives FY26 turnover of RM4,813.0m and FY25 of RM4,517.7m - matching the Results Highlights table and the company's own filing - but the Group Turnover row prints RM3,657.9m and RM3,408.3m. The same happens on EBIT: the segments sum to RM881.5m for FY26 and RM742.1m for FY25 against printed group figures of RM677.2m and RM565.2m. The quarterly columns in the same table do reconcile. (3) The Summary Earnings Table's valuation ratios appear struck at a lower share price than the RM3.70 on the cover - Core PER of 8.6x/8.8x/8.5x on core EPS of 40.2/39.4/40.8 sen implies about RM3.46-3.47, and PBV of 1.2x on BVPS of RM2.9 implies about RM3.48, while the page 5 peer table shows 9.4x and 9.1x at RM3.70. That implied price is arithmetic on the report's own numbers and is inferred, not stated. (4) The sum-of-parts table divides by 1,551m paid-up shares while the stock information box gives 1,556.3m shares outstanding, and takes the property segment at RM4,598m against the RM4,602m discounted RNAV computed in the following table. (5) The rating-definition box on page 6 defines OUTPERFORM and OVERWEIGHT as expected total return 'MORE than 1 %', where the same day's Kenanga Today prints 'MORE than 10%'.

Four points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The same number is used for two different things. The commentary says ‘exceptional sales were recorded in Malaysia at 3,433 units (+58%) which offset the weaker Philippines at 263 units (-43%)’, while the Unit Sales table gives 3,433 as the group total for 1QFY27 (Mazda 3,024 + Xpeng 409 + Kia nil) against 2,638 a year earlier, +30%. The two readings cannot both hold: a Malaysia-only 3,433 at +58% implies about 2,173 a year earlier, and adding the 263 Philippines units would put the group at 3,696 rather than 3,433. (2) The peer table's market capitalisation does not match the cover. The stock information box prints RM1,051.7m on 1,130.8m shares outstanding, which is what RM0.930 × 1,130.8m gives; the page 4 peer table prints RM1,079.7m for the same stock in the same document. The RM1,051.7m figure is the one the report's own share count supports - that reconciliation is computed here, not stated. (3) The dividend yield is quoted three ways. The cover and the investment case both say ‘attractive dividend yield of about 11%’, while the Summary Earnings Table prints FY27F Net Div. Yield of 10.5% and the peer table the same 10.5%; the trailing yield on the market-data source used for this row's yield column is 9.14%. (4) The peer table shows BAUTO's Current FYE as 04/2026 although the note reports 1QFY27 and forecasts FY27-FY28, and Kenanga's 52-week range (H RM1.10 / L RM0.49) differs slightly from the RM1.12 / RM0.50 on the market-data source feeding this row's range columns.

This is an Initiate Coverage report; it is filed here as a Company Update because this board's report-type dropdown is fixed to five types (rules/signals.md §6). There is no previous rating or previous target price, by definition. Four points of caution on the figures, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The report gives two different sets of WFE-exposure numbers. Page 1 says AMBEST's wafer-fab-equipment exposure is ‘projected to rise from approximately 47% of revenue in FY24 to some 70% by FY26’; page 8 says it will be ‘propelled from ~53% in FY2024 to ~76% by FY2027’, above an exhibit titled ‘We Estimate Ambest's WFE-Related Order to Account for ~65%/76% of Revenue in FY26/FY27’. FY24 appears as both 47% and 53%, FY26 as both 70% and 65%. The Edge Malaysia's 11 September report of this note carries the page-1 pair. (2) The financial year-end is labelled two ways. The front Summary Earnings Table says ‘FYE Dec’ and the page 13 peer table says ‘Current FYE 12/2026’, while the income statement, balance sheet, cash flow and ratio tables on page 12 all say ‘FYE May’. December is the reading the rest of the document supports - FY25 turnover of RM52.7m matches the trailing-twelve-month revenue on the market-data source, and 1HFY26 is already reported - but the note is not internally consistent and states no correction. (3) The front table's per-share figures are struck off a different profit line from the peer table's. The Summary Earnings Table shows FY26F Core EPS of 2.5 sen and Core PER of 60.1x, which at RM1.48 is FY26F net profit of RM12.6m over 510.0m shares; the FY26F core net profit of RM16.1m in the same column gives about 3.2 sen and about 47x on the same share base - and the peer table duly prints 3.0 sen and 49.0x. That reconciliation is arithmetic on the report's own numbers and is inferred, not stated. (4) The page 12 income statement has two row labels transposed: the ‘Associate’ row carries the PBT figures (9.0 / 8.2 / 7.5 / 16.6 / 46.0) and the ‘Exceptional Items’ row carries the taxation figures (2.2 / 1.1 / 1.1 / 4.1 / 9.4), each duplicating the correctly labelled row beneath it. The company is also named three ways in the same document - ‘AMBEST Berhad’ in the page headers, ‘AMBEST GROUP BHD’ in the peer table and ‘Ambest Precision Engineering Sdn. Bhd.’ in the company overview; the listed entity is Ambest Group Berhad.

Three points of caution on this row. (1) Two sentences in this note could be read as the pick declaration and they name different stocks. Page 1 says ‘We like IOICORP (OP; TP: RM5.40) and KLK (OP; TP:RM25.80) for the larger planters’; page 2 says ‘Our picks include IOICORP (OP; TP:RM5.40) for strong FY27 prospects...’. This board takes the page-2 sentence as the declaration, because under rules/signals.md §2 ‘we like’ on its own is an investment case rather than a pick. (2) The August CPO price of RM4,493 per MT needs care. Kenanga labels RM4,493 as the August price, +0.1% MoM and +9% YoY, which would put July at about RM4,489. The Edge Malaysia, in its 17-23 August 2026 weekly, reported the same RM4,493 per tonne as Malaysia's average CPO price for July, up 9.3% year on year. Kenanga's own 3 September report card, carried on this board, separately described CPO as having risen to RM4,612 in August - written before MPOB's August statistics were published. No independent MPOB average CPO price for August could be retrieved during this run, so all three prints are recorded here rather than one being chosen. (3) The note states ratings and target prices for IOICORP, KLK, PPB, HSPLANT, UMCCA, TSH, SDG, TAANN and GENP, none of which has a standalone Kenanga report in today's bundle; those figures are as quoted in this sector piece and have not been independently verified against stock-specific reports today. A smaller typographical point: the page-1 paragraph prints United Malacca's target as ‘TP:TM7.00’, given correctly as RM7.00 in the page-2 text and the peer table.

Eleven points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The bear-case de-rating for MAXIS is stated two ways. Page 1 says CDB’s asymmetric risk-reward holds ‘despite a more punitive bear case de-rating of -3SD (MAXIS: -2SD)’; pages 5 to 7 apply -1SD to MAXIS three times (‘for MAXIS... we assume a de-rating to -1SD’; ‘a de-rating to -1SD at 17.0x P/E’; ‘a de-rating to 17x (historical -1SD level)’). The -1SD reading is the one the rest of the document supports, since 17.0x is what produces the RM2.82/RM2.83 bear-case value. (2) MAXIS’s position against its own historical mean is stated two ways. Page 1: ‘it already trades at historical mean’. Page 5: ‘MAXIS, which is currently trading below its historical mean’. Page 6 gives 18.1x against a 19.7x mean, which is below it. (3) MAXIS’s bear-case value is printed twice at two figures - RM2.82 on page 6 and RM2.83 on page 7, both at 17.0x and both described as 20% downside; Exhibit 15 gives RM2.83. (4) The SWN announcement is dated two ways. Exhibit 1 and the page-2 text both put it in Mar 2021, but page 3 says MAXIS ‘remains 24% below its Sept-21 level, when SWN was first announced’. (5) MAXIS’s RM500m-scenario debt headroom does not match its own exhibit. The text gives RM3.01b; Exhibit 20 prints RM3,068m, which is also what RM3,568m less RM500m gives. The CDB equivalents reconcile exactly (RM1,546m/RM1,846m/RM2,046m against RM1.55b/RM1.85b/RM2.05b). (6) The 2026 DNB cash-commitment total does not add up from its own components. The text says ‘total annual cash commitments related to DNB in 2026 totalled RM528m p.a.’ while naming RM202m of April 2026 shareholders’ advances and RM328m for the MoF put option, which sum to RM530m (RM529.9m on Exhibit 16’s RM327.9m). (7) The headline scenario percentages are rounded in the text and precise in the exhibit: CDB +37%/-26% against Exhibit 13’s +36.6%/(25.5%), MAXIS +21%/-20% against +20.9%/(20.3%). (8) Exhibit 12’s caption contradicts the text - it reads ‘Bear −1SD / Bull: Hist. mean P/E’ for both stocks, though the text applies -3SD to CDB’s bear case. (9) CDB’s FY27F EPS appears as three figures: 12.7 sen in Exhibit 14’s 0% row, ‘13 sen’ in the stress-test text, and 12.8 sen in the peer table’s two-year forward core EPS. Related: the bear-case values cannot be reproduced from the stated multiple and base-case EPS alone - RM2.02 at 18.8x implies about 10.7 sen - because the bear case also assumes lower earnings; the note states the de-rating but never prints its bear-case EPS. That gap is identified here, not in the report. (10) The peer table’s price snapshot predates the same day’s digest. It shows AXIATA at RM1.68 and TELEKOM MALAYSIA at RM8.00, while Kenanga Today’s 11 September closes are RM1.71 and RM7.92. CDB’s RM2.72 and MAXIS’s RM3.54, used as ‘current share price’ throughout the note, do not appear in the digest’s tables and so could not be cross-checked. (11) Two sections are both numbered ‘(V)’, and this is filed as a Sector Update although the document is headed ‘Thematic Report’, because this board’s report-type dropdown is fixed to five types (rules/signals.md §6). It carries no ticker-level rating, target price or share price of its own, so those columns are empty by design. The divergence marker is deliberately not set: named houses do rate MAXIS opposite to Kenanga (see the analyst note), but this row carries no Kenanga rating of its own against which §3’s opposite-direction test can be applied.

Three points of caution on this row. (1) One sentence contradicts the note’s own table. The text reads ‘The population outside the labour force fell (0.01%; Jun: 0.09%) to 7.110m’, but Table 1 shows that population rising from 7,109.8k in June to 7,110.5k in July - an increase of about 0.01%, not a decrease. The table is the reading the rest of the document supports, since the labour force, employment and the participation rate all rose in the same month. Reported as printed. (2) This note and the Distributive Trade note published in the same bundle describe the same GDP figure differently. Here: ‘we raised our 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5.3% (2025: 5.2%)’. There: ‘we maintain our 2026 GDP growth forecast at 5.3% (2025: 5.2%)’. This board’s 1 September Manufacturing PMI row already carried 5.3% as the standing house forecast, which supports ‘maintain’. The number is identical in all three places, so there is no numerical contradiction to resolve - only the framing differs, and both are reproduced as printed. (3) Several typographical slips in the retrieved text are carried as printed: the title reads ‘Unemployment rate hold at 3.0%’, and the body contains ‘own-account workersup’, ‘for ther first time’, ‘Early September data warrant caution, The 3,128 cases...’ and ‘the ongoing the global E&E upcycle’.

Two points of caution on this row, both presentational rather than numerical - every figure quoted here reconciles against Table 1 of the note. (1) The same GDP figure is framed differently in the two Economic Viewpoints published in this bundle. This note says ‘we maintain our 2026 GDP growth forecast at 5.3% (2025: 5.2%)’; the Labour Market note says ‘we raised our 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5.3% (2025: 5.2%)’. This board’s 1 September Manufacturing PMI row already carried 5.3% as the standing house forecast, which supports the ‘maintain’ wording here. The number is the same in all three places, so nothing is in numerical conflict. (2) Typographical slips in the retrieved text, carried as printed: the title reads ‘Spending loss steam’ (for loses steam), a bullet reads ‘Broad-based moderation across sub-sector’, a sentence closes without its bracket (‘See Economic Viewpoint: Malaysia Distributive Trade’), the retail bullet runs two sentences together (‘(7.5%; Jun: 10.8%).Stronger sales...’), and the page-2 footer repeats a contact line followed by a stray ‘Head of Research’.

Five points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The peer average behind the target price cannot be reproduced from the report's own table. The TP is set at 37x FY27F PER, stated as a 10% discount to the average FY27 PER of 41.3x for local semiconductor front-end peers named as UWC, Frontken and Vitrox. But VITROX does not appear anywhere in the Malaysian Technology Peers Comparison on page 3, and the two named peers that do appear show two-year forward core PERs of 39.3x (UWC) and 31.7x (FRONTKEN), which average 35.5x rather than 41.3x. The 41.3x is therefore drawn from a peer set the document does not print. (2) KGB's own ROE is given two ways. The Financial Data & Ratios table on page 2 shows FY26F ROE of 24.5% and FY27F of 27.1%; the peer table on page 3 shows 27.8% for the one-year forward period, which every other column in that row (core EPS 21.7 sen, PBV 9.7x, net dividend 15.0 sen, yield 1.7%) identifies as FY26F. (3) The exchange rate implied by the contract conversion is not the one in the same day's digest. USD249.9m as c.RM1.01b and USD202.0m as c.RM817m both imply about RM4.04 to the dollar, against the 14 September USD/MYR fix of 4.0753 printed in Kenanga Today the same morning. (4) Earnings growth and EPS growth diverge sharply and the report does not explain why. Core net profit rises 30.6% in FY26F (RM151m to RM197m) while core EPS rises only 6.9% (20.3 sen to 21.7 sen), which implies the share base expands by roughly a fifth - about 744m shares implied for FY25A against about 908m for FY26F, versus 880.4m shares outstanding in the stock-information box. The report carries no note on share issuance, warrant conversion or dilution. This divergence is identified here, not in the report. (5) The 52-week range in Kenanga's own stock-information box (H RM9.20, L RM4.75) differs from the market data used in this row's range columns (stockanalysis.com: RM9.25 / RM4.70).

Six points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) One target price disagrees with this board's own earlier row. The note prints CIMB as (OP; TP: RM8.30); this board's 1 September Results Note on CIMB, read from CIMB's own report PDF, carries OUTPERFORM with a target of RM8.35. The five-sen gap cannot be resolved from the retrieved sources and neither figure is used as this row's data - the row carries no rating or target of its own. (2) The MGS baseline is given two ways on the same page. Page 2 states that 10-year MGS yields 'had spiked from 3.7% to the current more than 4.1%' on BNM information, while the sensitivity analysis in the same section assumes yields 'rising to c4.1%, versus 3.6% as at end of 2Q26'. A 3.7% or a 3.6% starting point changes the size of the revaluation being estimated. (3) The KLFIN decline is given two ways. Page 1: the index 'has slipped more than 2% since end-August'. Page 2: 'almost 3% KLFIN dip since August'. Both are reproduced. (4) The stated devaluation and the stated ringgit amount do not quite agree. A 'c2% devaluation' applied to a RM126b FVTPL book is described as amounting to RM2.3b; RM2.3b on RM126b is 1.83%. The gap is within the note's own 'roughly estimate' framing but is identified here, not in the document. (5) Two exhibit cross-references point at the wrong exhibits. The text directs the reader to 'exhibit 1' for the December 2026, June 2027 and December 2027 futures contracts - that chart is Exhibit 10, while Exhibit 1 is the banks' fixed-income securities table - and to 'exhibit 4' for the technology sector's negative correlation with oil, which is Exhibit 12, while Exhibit 4 is the fixed-deposit maturity mix. (6) The note quotes ratings and target prices for stocks that have no standalone report in this day's bundle - MAYBANK, HLBANK, ABMB, CIMB, MISC, PCHEM, WPRTS, SUNREIT, PAVREIT and KPJ. Those figures are as quoted in this strategy piece and have not been independently verified against stock-specific reports today; where this board holds an earlier Kenanga row for the same stock the two agree, except for CIMB as set out in point (1).

Four points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) A forecast is maintained and qualified in the same sentence. The note states 'We maintain our year-end USDMYR forecast of 3.95 but see 4.00 as the more realistic near-term anchor' - so the published forecast and the number the note actually expects are different, and the spot fix printed in the same morning's digest is 4.0857. Both are carried as printed. (2) One rate forecast is acknowledged as already overtaken. The end-2026 10-Y UST forecast of 4.80% is described in the note itself as sitting below spot and dependent on oil retracing, with risks 'clearly skewed higher' and a sustained break above 5.00% forcing a revision. It is carried here as the standing house number while the note itself flags it as under pressure. (3) The house call for this meeting was wrong and the note says so. Table 3 records the KIBB Research Outlook for the 15-16 September meeting as 'No change' against a Fed Funds futures reading of a 25bps hike and an actual 25bps hike, and the text states 'We expected a hold and were wrong on the meeting.' Recorded as printed; this is Kenanga's own correction, not a discrepancy identified here. (4) Two different oil benchmarks appear across the day's bundle. This note cites Brent above USD100; the same morning's digest prints Nymex crude oil at USD105.8 a barrel, up 4.38%. They are different contracts and are not in conflict, but they are not the same number and no Brent figure of its own is printed anywhere in the note.

Seven points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The day's published bundle is two reports short of the day's advertised line-up. Both the digest's Ideas of the Day and Kenanga's own Kenanga Today page for 18 September name Economic Viewpoint: Bond Market Weekly Outlook, Ringgit Weekly Outlook alongside this Company Update and a Rating Summary - but the published bundle contains only the digest and this report. Both Economic Viewpoints returned HTTP 404 under every filename convention this board knows, including the exact patterns that worked for the same two titles on 28 August, 4 September and 7 September. They are excluded on the authority of the bundle contents, the same treatment given BIMB on 27 August. Rating Summary is excluded by specification. This day therefore carries one report row, not three. (2) The headline discount is measured against book value, but the text applies it to the market. Exhibit 1 compares realisable value of RM1,358.0m to a PPE carrying value of RM961.8m for a discount of 29.2% - which reconciles exactly. The text, however, says the market 'currently prices the stock at a 30% discount' and that 'the market is mispricing the company by 29.2% based on its fleet's realizable value alone'. Market capitalisation is RM1,083.0m in the note's own Stock Information box, which against RM1,358.0m is a 20.3% discount, not 29.2% - arithmetic here, and identified here rather than in the document. (3) The payback claim does not reconcile to the PPE figure used elsewhere in the note. The text states that on FY26F earnings of RM72m the group 'would be able to breakeven on its PPE value in 12 years'. RM72m into the RM961.8m of Exhibit 1 is 13.4 years; 12 years reconciles instead to the RM861m of FY2025 fixed assets in the note's own balance sheet. Both computations are arithmetic here.
